brief.headline: Defensives lead, tech breaks, ASML and INTC demand attention
brief.regime_summary: SPY is labeled risk-on but the tape is sending mixed signals. The index sits just 0.05% above its 50DMA after a 0.71% weekly loss and a 1.58% one-month decline. VIX at 16.95 is below its 20DMA of 17.73, suggesting vol is contained rather than elevated. Breadth is acceptable, with 63.6% of sectors above their 50DMAs, but sector momentum tells a cleaner story: XLP, XLV, and XLRE lead the 20-day rankings, while XLK sits dead last at -12.4%. A Democratic midterm result, per WSJ, is adding noise to the AI trade. This is risk-on in label only. Treat defensive sector leadership and tech underperformance as a regime warning until XLK stabilizes.

portfolio.note: Up 4.67% on the week, 4.68% above its 20DMA, RSI 64.3. Relative volume of 2.1x confirms genuine interest. At a 35.6% unrealized gain, no thesis change, but RSI approaching overbought territory and XLK is the weakest sector. Watch the 20DMA near $530 as a reversion anchor.

Down 10% on the week, 18.7% off its 20-day high, RSI 34.9, full bearish MA stack. EPS estimates are actually rising (19 upgrades, zero cuts in 30 days, +5.1% revision) and forward PE of 23.6x is 6.2% below historical median, so the fundamental case has not broken. The price action has. The midterm result adds export-control uncertainty to semis. Thesis is intact but technicals are deteriorating; worth reviewing position sizing at this ATR (4.05%, or roughly $60 per share).
Down 7.2% on the week, 5.85% below its 20DMA, RSI 38.9. WTI crude fell 11.8% in the same period, which explains the move. The 100DMA at roughly $61.14 is the next meaningful support level to watch.

Essentially flat on the week (-0.27%), RSI 47.8, only 0.28% below the 20DMA. The bearish MA stack on gold futures (GC=F) persists with a -1.31% gap to the 40DMA, but the ETF is holding up relatively well. A 61.9% unrealized gain makes this a low-urgency position; monitor the 40DMA area for any further slippage.

watchlist.name: Accenture plc
watchlist.thesis: Up 8.57% on the week, 11.37% above its 20DMA, 47.4% above its 100DMA. Twenty-day momentum is 35.5%, forty-day is 51.5%. ACN is outperforming its sector by 47.8% on a 20-day basis, which is exceptional. Trailing PE of 19.5x is 12.4% above its historical median but forward PE is 16.6x on 4.96% EPS growth. Earnings are December 17, leaving several weeks of runway. The setup is extended; a pullback toward the 20DMA near $237 would offer a cleaner entry risk.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $237.29, 20-day high: $267.47, ATR-based stop: ~1.0 ATR ($10.92) below entry
watchlist.risk: Setup breaks if the XLK tape deteriorates further or if December earnings guidance disappoints.

watchlist.name: Gilead Sciences
watchlist.thesis: Up 9.6% on the week, 10.2% above its 20DMA, RSI 73.3. EPS revision of +148% over 30 days is the most dramatic estimate change in the screen. Revenue estimates are also rising (+1.84%). Earnings have already passed (reported October 29), removing event risk for now. Healthcare (XLV) is the second-strongest sector on 20-day momentum, providing a supportive backdrop.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: implied near $158, 20-day high: within 0.67% of current price, ATR-based stop: ~1.0 ATR (2.77%) below entry
watchlist.risk: RSI at 73 means the name is stretched; a rotation out of defensives would hit XLV names quickly.

watchlist.name: Intuitive Surgical
watchlist.thesis: Up 8.54% on the week, 10.3% above its 20DMA, RSI 72.6. EPS estimates revised up 4.19%, revenue up 1.45%. PE vs history is -23.9%, meaning it trades 24% below its own median multiple despite 26% expected EPS growth this year. Next earnings January 21 provides time. Volume at 1.82x average supports the move.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: implied near $437, 20-day high: within 0.77% of current, ATR-based stop: ~1.0 ATR (3.14%) below entry
watchlist.risk: High trailing PE of 58.3x is a valuation anchor; any risk-off rotation or earnings preannouncement ends the setup.

watchlist.name: Home Depot
watchlist.thesis: Up 11.9% on the week, 12.6% above its 20DMA, RSI 74.5. News flow ties the move to post-midterm housing optimism. Earnings are November 17, twelve days away. The move is large and the RSI is at an extreme; at the same time, XLY momentum is positive and the thesis around housing activity is real. This is a watch-into-earnings setup, not a chase.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: implied near $316, 20-day high: within 0.16% of current, ATR-based stop: ~1.0 ATR (2.48%) below entry
watchlist.risk: Earnings on November 17 could snap back all of the anticipatory move if guidance disappoints.

watchlist.name: Caterpillar
watchlist.thesis: Down 17.1% on the week, 16.5% below its 20DMA, RSI 23.0. The stock is 27.9% off its 20-day high with bearish MA stack at all three moving average levels and a 20-day momentum of -27.2%. EPS estimates are only modestly revised (+0.61%) so estimates have not fully caught up to the price action. Industrials (XLI) is the second-weakest sector. This is not an oversold bounce setup in a tape where the sector is already lagging.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: implied near $706, 20-day high: $820, ATR-based stop: ~1.0 ATR (5.0%) above entry for a short
watchlist.risk: RSI at 23 is deeply oversold; a short squeeze or any positive macro catalyst in industrials could produce a sharp counter-trend move.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: Down 39% on the week, 48% below its 20-day high, RSI 22.8. The stock is 33.96% below its 20DMA and 43.5% below its 100DMA. EPS and revenue estimates are both being cut (-2.44% and -2.06% respectively). Annualized volatility of 128.9% makes this a high-risk name regardless of direction. News cites chip sector weakness and PC market share concerns. No earnings until January 28.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $88.24, 20-day high: $111.60, ATR-based stop: ~1.0 ATR ($6.42) above entry for a short
watchlist.risk: At this level of oversold, any acquisition rumor or government contract news could trigger a violent short-covering rally given extreme volatility.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: Down 11.8% on the week to $89.93, RSI 40.8, sitting 8.3% below its 20DMA and 18.6% off the 20-day high. The long-term 100DMA is still supportive (+3.2% above), but the near-term momentum of -1.71% over 20 days is rolling over. Watch $87-88 as the next area; a break there would pressure XLE further.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Up 2.4% on the week to $4,128, RSI 51.1, sitting just 0.97% above its 20DMA. The bearish MA stack persists on the 40 and 100DMA comparisons, but the weekly gain amid equity weakness suggests some safe-haven demand is returning. A close above the 40DMA is the level to watch for trend confirmation.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Down 2.65% on the week to $6.41, RSI 43.3, 1.97% below its 20DMA. Mixed MA stack and anomalously high relative volume (8.7x) on a down week warrants attention as a leading indicator for global industrial demand. Continued weakness here would validate the CAT and XLI bearish thesis.

commodities.name: Corn
commodities.note: RSI at 28.1, down 10.8% over 20 days and 11.6% from its 20-day high. Oversold but with no catalyst visible. Thin relative volume (0.08x) means price discovery is poor; not a tradeable setup yet.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.note: Effectively flat on the week (-0.44%) at $2.939 with RSI at 50.3, sitting just 0.51% below the 20DMA. Mixed MA stack and high volatility (50.1% annualized). Neutral for now; watch for winter demand signals in coming weeks.
